Change c0240. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. XII.

Context before (unchanged): "I spent the winter in this manner.

1818 text: The gentle manners and beauty of the cottagers greatly endeared them to me: when they were unhappy, I felt depressed; when they rejoiced, I sympathized in their joys.

1831 text: The gentle manners and beauty of the cottagers greatly endeared them to me: when they were unhappy, I felt depressed; when they rejoiced, I sympathised in their joys.

Diff: The gentle manners and beauty of the cottagers greatly endeared them to me: when they were unhappy, I felt depressed; when they rejoiced, I [-sympathized-] {+sympathised+} in their joys.

Context after (unchanged): I saw few human beings beside them; and if any other happened to enter the cottage, their harsh manners and rude gait only enhanced to me the superior accomplishments of my friends.

result.rationale: Only the orthography changes: 'sympathized' becomes 'sympathised' (-ize to -ise). The wording and meaning of 'sympathised in their joys' are unchanged.
